clue.text: African people talked about ZSL facilities?

indicators.note: something talked about is spoken, so we want a word that matches the sound of the phrase that follows

parts.note: ZSL is the Zoological Society of London, which runs London Zoo; its facilities are zoo loos (toilets)

explanation.surface: A query about whether some African people discussed the amenities at London Zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: ZSL stands for the Zoological Society of London; 'facilities' is a polite word for toilets, a loo in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zulus are a Bantu-speaking nation of southern Africa, chiefly KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: Man at the outset thinks: might youth mess with booze?

parts.note: mankind as a whole, ourselves: we

indicators.note: at the outset points to the very start of the next word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of thinks
might, in the sense of being able or allowed to, is can
a youth is a teen

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether young people ought to be fooling about with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' is not a verb here but the military dining room; a wet canteen is a forces bar where alcohol is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet canteen is a service canteen or mess licensed to sell alcoholic drink, as opposed to a dry one.

clue.text: Wroxham and Malthouse? We may lead you there!

parts.note: surface reading: two English places or perhaps people, Wroxham village and a Malthouse
setter's reading: Wroxham and Malthouse are Norfolk lakes, and these lakes, speaking for themselves, lead you into the whole waterway region of the same name

explanation.surface: Two Norfolk names apparently boast that they can guide a visitor to some destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Wroxham Broad and Malthouse Broad are lakes in the Norfolk Broads, a waterway network in eastern England popular for boating holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is a broad, a shallow lake formed from old peat diggings, and together such lakes form the region.

clue.text: Following set-up, pinch and take home skittle

indicators.note: in a down clue being set up means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters run upward, the other way round

parts.note: to pinch is to nip
to take home pay is to net it

explanation.surface: Instructions for a bowling-style game: after the pins are arranged, nick one and carry it home.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenpin is one of the ten pins knocked down in tenpin bowling, a kind of skittle.

clue.text: Badly unillumined line overlooked by penetrating earthly light

indicators.note: penetrating means going right inside, so one piece is placed within the other
something done badly is botched, so the remaining letters come out in a jumbled order
what is overlooked gets ignored, so those letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed
by as in multiplication, the times sign x

explanation.surface: A poorly lit line of text is overlooked, while some worldly light breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: By is the multiplication sign, as in three by four; overlooked asks for a word to be left out of a longer one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lux mundi is Latin for 'light of the world', a title of Christ, so a light belonging to the earth.

clue.text: One heartlessly has children in the firing line?

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other
without its heart, the word loses its central letter and keeps only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of one
ch is the standard abbreviation for children or child

explanation.surface: A cruel person puts children in danger, standing in the line of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: darts players throw from behind the oche.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw, so the line darts are fired from.

clue.text: Resort northern? To be sure, a southern resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for northern
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a holiday resort is in the north and is told no, it is a southern one.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Resort' looks like the definition but is the instruction to re-sort letters; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a seaside town on the Sussex coast of southern England.

clue.text: Ill-deserved smacker possibly rejected by native

indicators.note: something rejected is cast out, so this letter is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: native in the sense of innate, inborn, not acquired by study
a smacker is slang for a pound, and L is the pound sign's letter

explanation.surface: A local person turns away an undeserved kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Smacker suggests a kiss, but here it is slang for a pound, abbreviated L (from libra).
explanation.definitionFit: Something unearned has not been worked for, so it is not deserved.

clue.text: Props loading one crateful after another

indicators.note: after sets the order, the second copy following straight on from the first
only the part of the load visible at the join is kept, the rest of each case being dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a second crateful following the first

explanation.surface: Stagehands carry props, one crateful following the next.
explanation.walkthrough: Write crateful twice in a row: the letters straddle the join, the end of one crateful and the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulcra, plural of fulcrum, are the supports on which levers pivot, so props in the sense of supports.

clue.text: Part of organ at the end of Viz strip

indicators.note: placing one thing at the end of another fixes their order, the first piece following the second

parts.note: viz and sc (scilicet) are both abbreviations meaning namely
a reed is a type of pipe in an organ

explanation.surface: A bit of a church organ appears in the last panel of a comic strip from Viz.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is a British adult comic, which makes 'strip' look like a cartoon; here viz is the abbreviation for namely.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a strip of plaster or wood laid as a guide to level a floor or wall.

clue.text: Loose snake accounting for pawnbroker's right hand

indicators.note: accounting for here means disposing of, so one piece takes over the place of a letter
the right hand of a word as written is its final letter, the one to be swapped out

parts.note: uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: An escaped snake is the reason a pawnbroker's right hand has been bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'right hand' of the word for a pawnbroker is its last letter, E, which the snake replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to unfasten or release it, the same as to unclasp.

clue.text: How French, this remark

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French word for how
second meaning: an observation in English

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how very French a particular comment sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling is the French interrogative 'how' and the English noun for an observation.

clue.text: Way back, just after dipping into single chapter novel

indicators.note: to dip into something is to go inside it, so one piece is set within the other
novel means new, so the letters before it are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: on as in on arrival, immediately after
taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having dipped into a one-chapter novel a while ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Long since means a long time ago, the same as way back in casual speech.

clue.text: Pilot dons seductive glossy material

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as clothing, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: luring means enticing, seductive
a pilot study is a test

explanation.surface: An airline pilot puts on some alluring shiny fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot looks like a person, but it is the adjective-turned-noun for a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutestring is a lustrous silk fabric, once used for dresses and ribbons.

clue.text: Returning zero fish caught in sea trip, one could deal blow

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read from the other end

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
a cran is a measure of herrings landed, a quantity of fish brought in from a fishing trip

explanation.surface: A fishing boat comes back with no catch, and someone is ready to lash out.
explanation.walkthrough: Blow is slang for cocaine, so the definition is a drug dealer, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A narco is a drug trafficker, someone who might deal cocaine, called blow in slang.

clue.text: Doctor and Master characters brought together complex storylines?

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them
MA is a Master of Arts
characters in a play are roles

explanation.surface: Doctor Who and his foe the Master are brought together in a convoluted plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Doctor Who, whose villain is called the Master; the question mark marks the loose definition of long-winded tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, rambling and confused account, so a tangled story.

clue.text: Show these people question is gender fluid

indicators.note: something fluid flows and changes shape, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: these people are them
to question is to ask
the letters of is gender, rearranged

explanation.surface: A demonstration that some people are asking whether gender is fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masked Singer is a TV talent show in which celebrities sing in costume, hiding their identity.

clue.text: Needs an operative to cover current bases

indicators.note: to cover something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other
an operative letter set is one that is worked on, so it gets rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A spy is required to keep watch over military bases currently in use.
explanation.walkthrough: Operative looks like a secret agent; it is the anagram signal, and bases are chemical, not military.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenine is one of the four nucleobases in DNA and RNA, so adenines are bases.

clue.text: Picked up fragments after rolling one kilo butt in

indicators.note: after sets the order, so the sounded piece follows the rolled one
rolling turns something over, so the letters come back the other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
K is the abbreviation for kilo

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: fragments are bits, spelt here as it sounds

explanation.surface: Someone gathers broken pieces after a one-kilogram thing tumbles into a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: To kibitz is to offer unwanted advice or interfere, from Yiddish, so to butt in.

clue.text: Toast success in Geneva's banks

indicators.note: banks contain a river, so the letters are held within the words before

parts.note: run on from the end of success through in to the start of Geneva's

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to success in the banking world of Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: Toast looks like a celebratory drink, but it is the verb for browning; Geneva is famous for Swiss banking.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to brown it with heat, as to singe is to scorch lightly.

clue.text: Make retrospective claim first off, and refuse to go ahead

indicators.note: to go ahead puts the second piece in front of the first in the finished word

parts.note: bran is husks, waste or refuse from grain

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word is read from end to start
first off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: Someone first makes a claim backdated and then declines to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: Make is a noun here, as in the make of a car; refuse is a noun too, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A make of product is its brand name, the trade name under which it is sold.

clue.text: A misleadingly named fillet

indicators.note: something presented misleadingly is distorted, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of named, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cut of meat sold under a deceptive label.
explanation.walkthrough: Fillet looks like a cut of beef or fish; here it is a band worn round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or headband, and a fillet is a narrow band worn around the hair.

clue.text: Bumper celebration for one daughter about to get married

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the preceding letters run the other way

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A huge party is held for a daughter who is about to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumper looks like an adjective meaning huge, tying it to the celebration; it is the noun for a fairground car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a small electric car at a fairground, built to bump into others.

clue.text: Poet on radio mocking suspension

indicators.note: something on radio is only heard, so the word is judged by sound alone

parts.note: mocking or ironic is wry
mist is fine water droplets suspended in the air

explanation.surface: A poet on the radio pokes fun at someone being suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspension is the scientific sense, droplets held in air, not a ban or a car part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymist is a writer of rhymes, a versifier, so a poet, though usually a humble one.

clue.text: Tubers heading for Stanmore might, on northbound route

indicators.note: in a down clue travelling northbound means going up the column, so the letters read from bottom to top
the heading of a word is its top, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Stanmore
might and may both express possibility

explanation.surface: Underground trains might head north towards Stanmore, terminus of London's Jubilee line.
explanation.walkthrough: Tubers puns on the Tube, London's Underground; Stanmore is the northern end of the Jubilee line.
explanation.definitionFit: Yams are the starchy edible tubers of a tropical climbing plant.

clue.text: I could mention more at another time having cross to bear

indicators.note: having means holding, so one piece is carried inside the other

parts.note: anon means soon or at some other time
the Distinguished Service Order is a military decoration in the form of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone hints that there is more to say later, given a burden they carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross to bear sounds like a burden; it is a medal, the DSO, a British gallantry decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: And so on is said in place of listing further items, as a speaker could go on but does not.

clue.text: Signatory brings Western powers together

indicators.note: the first word brings the letters with it, carrying them inside itself

parts.note: the middle letters of signatory

explanation.surface: A treaty signatory unites the powers of the West.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a statement about treaties, which suits the alliance itself.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance of Western countries.

clue.text: Recognised group of people more affected by shock?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: comparative of numb, read as more numb

explanation.surface: A query whether a known set of people was more traumatised than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the word read with a silent b as numb plus er, rather than the usual count word.
explanation.definitionFit: A number can be a group, as in one of our number, and numb with er means more deadened by shock.

clue.text: Showing respect at all times during split

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone stays respectful throughout a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means feeling or showing deep respect, as in a reverent hush.
